ports.description: Use the Action List Item to trigger an action directly from a list

Each screen of a mobile application is typically represented by a 'Page' consisting of a header, a scrollable content area and optionally a footer. The standard header offers a navigation button and a title. Alternatively you can provide a customer header. Gernerally you should use Toolbars in the Page. If you need a centered title you may use a Bar.
Breadcrumbs is useful for displaying link hierarchy
A Busy Dialog blocks the user interface until the currently running operation has been finished. No other activities can be started in parallel.
Buttons trigger user actions and come in a variety of shapes and colors. Placing a button on a page header or footer changes its appearance.
With the Carousel a user can browse through multi-page content by swiping left or right.
In this sample, the CheckBox reflects the selection states of its dependent input fields - selected, not selected, and partially selected.
The standalone ColorPalette in a container (sap.ui.layout.SimpleForm).

The table shares many features with the list and, in addition, introduces columns. The table is fully responsive and can hide columns or shown them in-place if the screen space is not sufficient. This example also demonstrates the different table pop-in layout options along with sticky column headers, header toolbar and info toolbar options.
The following example simulates a click on a list item in a table.
The combo box control provides a list box with items and a text field allowing the user to either type a value directly into the control or choose from the list of existing items.

The pattern allows users to select multiple items from an sap.m.Table and display information about them in a structured way - all items are displayed next to each other for easy comparison, based on their specifics.
The Cookie Settings Dialog allows you to easily manage the cookie settings according to the needs of the specific product.
With the Custom List Item you can add any kind of content to lists.
With the Custom Tree Item you can add any kind of content to Tree.
This example shows Date Picker which is opened by another control.
The Date Range Selection is an extension of the Date Picker Control and enables the user to select range of dates.
With the DateTimePicker a Date can be entered or selected including the time part.
Creating a dialog with confirm and reject options that replaces the confirmDialog functionality.
Use the Display List Item for showing name/value pairs.
The Draft Indicator shows that eighter currently a draft is saving or that it is already saved. It does not block the current UI screen so other operations could be triggered in parallel.
This is a 'Light' version of the Facet Filter. It is for small displays where only a selectable summary bar is shown, and a dialog is shown for setting the facet values.
Shows the tile containing the text of the feed, a subheader, and a numeric value.
This sample shows you how to build a complete feed user interface by combining a FeedInput with a list of FeedListItems.
The Feed List Item provides a standard UI for 'feeds' where multiple users publish information on regular basis on a certain topic.
Flex Boxes can be nested. Remember also that HBox and VBox are 'convenience' controls based on the Flex Box control.
Previews of the GenericTag control based on combinations of different sets of properties.
Shows KPI Tile samples that can contain header, subheader, key value, trend, scale, unit, and a footer.
The Header Container with horizontal layout. It provides horizontal scrolling on mobile devices (tablet and phone). On a desktop, it provides scroll left and scroll right buttons.

In this example, the IconTabBar height is stretched to the maximum height of the page content. Note: The height of the parent container must be defined as a fixed value. Also, applyContentPadding property is set to false and backgroundDesign property is set to Transparent.
Visualizes the state of the control when the mode property is set to ImageMode.Background.
This example shows different input value states.
Usually you use an Object Identifier in the first column of a table. But if you need an active identifier you should use an 'emphasized' link instead.
The counter of an item quickly shows how many detail entries are related, without having to navigate to the detail page.
If the list is empty it indicates this state by displaying a message text.
Shows how to set initial focus to MessageBox button.
The Message Toast displays the message text as an overlay to the current screen. It closes automatically after some time without requiring further user interaction.
A sample showing how you can connect the MessageView with MessageManager.
Items in the MultiComboBox could be grouped by a property
MultiInput provides functionality to add / remove / enter tokens.

This is a Object Header which displays the basic information about objects similar to the Object List Item. Besides a title and number you can show multiple attributes (on the left) and statuses (on the right).
The object status is a small building block representing a status with a semantic color.
Panels also have the possibility to expand/collapse their content (including the infoToolbar if available). [since rel. 1.22]
A PDF viewer opening as a popup dialog.
With the RangeSlider a user can specify range from a numerical interval.
The Scroll Container is a control that can display arbitrary content within a limited screen area and provides touch scrolling to make all content accessible.

The Segmented Button allows the user to pick one out of many options for displaying the content of the current page. It is a UI pattern from iOS, now also available for other platforms. Putting the Segmented Button to a Bar control on non-iOS platforms will result in something very close to a tab.
Illustrates the usage of a Select in header, footer and content of a page. Note the different display options.
The StepInput allows the user to change stepwise a value by a predefined step and also to set additional description, such as units of measurement and currencies after the input field.
"Some say it is only a switch, I say it is one of the most stylish controls in the universe of mobile UI controls." (unknown developer)
The text control can be used for embedding longer paragraphs of text into your application, that need text wrapping.
The Text Area allows to enter multi-line text and automatically breaks to a new line for overflow text. If the text gets too big to be displayed at once the user can scroll up and down.
Toolbar items can shrink/expand when the toolbar is resized. This behavior is enabled/disabled via the ToolbarLayoutData layout. It is also possible to set min/max width for shrinkable items.
Tree displays data in hierarchical structure.
Icon Tab Header used standalone, outside of Icon Tab Bar.
Shows ImageContent that can include an icon, a profile image, or a logo with a tooltip.
Use the Input List Item on phones to build form like user interfaces.
This sample shows the different behaviors of a label.
Displays several image thumbnails. Clicking on each of them will open a LightBox.
This control is used to show a menu in both desktop and mobile.
This control is used to open a menu in both desktop and mobile.
A sample MessageStrip that shows status messages with additional formatting.
This control is used to display the news content text and subheader in a tile.
Shows NumericContent including an icon.
The message handling concept sample shows how you can connect an error inside the page (such as input validation error) with an error, visualized as an item in a message popover.

MessagePopover is a control that displays a summarized list of different types of messages (errors, warnings, success and information). It provides a handy and systemized way to navigate and explore details for every message.
The message handling concept sample shows how you can use callback functions for resolving a promise after a link or descriptions have been asynchronously validated.
With the Slider a user can choose a value from a numerical range.

Typically the Radio Button is used by other controls. E.g. the List uses it for the single selection. But you can also use the Radio Buttons control directly, to allow selection of exactly one of multiple options.
Shows the progress of a process in a graphical way. To indicate the progress, the inside of the ProgressIndicator is filled with a color.
The object identifier is a small building block representing an object by a title and short description. Often it is used in the first column of a table.
The object number is a small building block representing an important, numerical attribute of an object together with it's unit. Often it is used in the last column of a table.
This is an example of Object Attribute used standalone.
The Object List Item has many possibilities to provide a quick overview for an object within a list.
A SelectList allows the user to select one item from a list of choices.
A list item suitable for showing notifications to the user.
A control suitable for grouping notifications.
Shows the universal container for different content types and context information in the footer area.
This sample shows how to add a link to a title.
Toggle Buttons can be toggled between pressed and normal state.

With the Pull to Refresh you can trigger an update operation by swiping the current page down on touch devices. On other devices the Pull To Refresh is visible all the time and the user clicks it like a button.
Shows Generic Tile with the 2x1 frame type displayed as sliding tiles.
This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with title, description, and avatar.
The URL Helper can be used to easily trigger a phone's native apps like Email, Telephone and SMS. It can be used with any UI control but typically an active Display List Item is chosen.
Basic Tokenizer with tokens
The Design and Style properties can be used to specify the visual design of the OverflowToolbar/Toolbar.

Many UI5 containers support the standard container content padding CSS classes. Apply the CSS class 'sapUiNoContentPadding' on a UI5 container control to remove the default padding around the container content area.

Use standard margin classes 'sapUiTinyMargin', 'sapUiSmallMargin', 'sapUiMediumMargin' or 'sapUiLargeMargin' to add a 8px (0.5rem), 16px (1rem), 32px (2rem) or 48px (3rem) margin to your control. This will clear the area all around your control (outside its border).

This page implements the same sample as in 'Fiori Sample Page - sapUiFioriObjectPage' using standard margin classes. In contrast to using 'sapUiFioriObjectPage', the margins used for form, list, table and panel are responsive: they adapt to the available screen width. For more information, please search for 'Standard Margins' and take a look at our samples.
Use a Search Field inside a Dialog.
This example demonstrates the Time Picker that is opened by another control.
This example demonstrates the automatic pop-in behavior of the table and hiding columns instead of moving them into the pop-in depending on their importance.
The sap.m.TabContainer allows for working with multiple tabs.

In some cases the closing behavior of the Popover can lead to drill down navigation. This sample demonstrates how you can control this. When the Popover is opened, add a style "pointer-events: none" to the area that should remain static and when the Popover is closed, remove it. Please note that, when having nested controls with "pointer-events" set, depending on the value of the property, internal controls may fire events, which will bubble up and trigger other events where applicable. The application needs to handle such cases.
TimePickerSliders used in a Dialog.

SplitContainer maintains two NavContainers if running on tablet or desktop and one NavContainer - on phone. The display of master NavContainer depends on the portrait/landscape orientation of the device and the mode of SplitContainer.
The SplitApp is the base for each master detail application. It extends the sap.m.SplitContainer control.
The View Settings Dialog is a standard UI pattern for specifying sorting, grouping and filtering.
QuickViewCard embedded in container
QuickView basic samples.
The Wizard is useful for breaking down complex tasks into smaller steps.

The sample demonstrates how to rebind a control to a different data source after a certain delay. This is useful when working with data that may change dynamically, as it allows the control to automatically update its displayed value without the need for user interaction.

The Select Dialog allows the user to search for and pick an item from a possibly long option list. Basically it is a convenience function to quickly assemble a Dialog, a Search Field and a List with Standard List Items. You can have single select or multi select mode. The dialog can remember the selections previously set on the dialog.

Similar to the Select Dialog, the Table Select Dialog presents selectable items in a table-based dialog, with filter functions. You can have single select or multi select mode. The dialog can remember the selections previously set on the dialog.
Semantic Page Full Screen
Integration of Floating Footer inside Semantic Page
Semantic Page Master/Detail
PlanningCalendar with only one row without row header.  On click on an interval a new appointment is created.
SinglePlanningCalendar with multiple date selection functionality.
Shell Bar example showing the control title as part of a mega menu, configurable by the app developer.
Basic example of Color Picker. Note that you have to set the Color Picker mode to HSL to take advantage of the responsiveness of the control on a mobile device.
InfoLabel with all available color schemes
Display or edit source code with syntax highlighting for various source types.
Basic example showing most controls which are intended to be used inside a table.
This example shows subsections in expanded and collapsed mode.
This sample illustrates how to specify the predefined header and the content of the Card control.
Different types of cards types arranged in a sap.f.GridContainer.
Shows a FixFlex control with a vertical layout.
With the HTML controls you can easily embed any kind of HTML content into your UI5 mobile application.
This sample shows an Upload Set control with a list of files to be uploaded and actions you can perform on them.
Built with an embedded font, icons scale well, and can be altered with CSS. They can also fire a press event. See the Icon Explorer for more icons.
Navigation List in a Page
CSSGrid example for page layout.
Simple splitter example with two content areas
Basic File Uploader Example

Many controls provide the associations ariaLabelledBy and ariaDescribedBy for accessibility purposes. The InvisibleText control can be used by application to provide hidden texts on the UI which can be referenced via these associations.
SideNavigation in container with fixed width.
Formats and parses only the integer digits. The decimal digits are ignored.
A control's busy indicator can be used to block parts of the screen until an operation has finished. In this example we block the content of only one out of two panels.
Sample provides a link to the Theme Parameter Toolbox. There you can easily search, preview, and filter semantic theme parameters.
SideNavigation with tags for status indicators and metadata.
This is a sample for GridList with different modes of selection.
ToolHeader that mimics the content of the Shell.

Formats the number by using the parameters defined for the given currency code. Either currency symbol, currency code or none of them can be included in the final formatted string. It parses the given string into an array which contains both the currency number and currency code.
Demonstrates the usage of Side Panel with single action item.
Example for multi-header of table

Attaches side content area which is next to the main content of the page on larger screens taking different ratios between the two on different screen sizes and on phone size screens the side content area falls down under the main content area. Best viewed in full screen.
Calendar where the user can select a single day
Block Layout in which all cells use the same background color set and different color shade.
The InvisibleMessage provides a way to programmaticaly expose dynamic content changes in a way that can be announced by screen readers.
A form that uses Toolbars as Form header and FormContainer headers.
InfoLabel used as subheader in DynamicPage
This layout allows to display same height grid items with configurable width.
Example of setting the gridAutoFlow property.
This sample demonstrates usage of the Hyphenation API
A busy indicator can be used to block the entire screen until an operation has finished.
This sample represents GridList with enabled Drag and Drop functionality.
Card Explorer is the application where you can learn more about integration cards.
Example how to use CodeEditor with IconTabHeader to create a tab-based experience.
islamic Calendar with secondary gregorian type
Shell Bar example with a menu button and a plain title.
The sap.m.MaskInput control allows users to easily enter data in a certain format and in a fixed-width input (for example: date, time, credit card number, and others).
The control can be used for embedding formatted HTML text into your application.
Checkboxes allow users to select a subset of options. If you want to offer an off/on setting you should use the Switch control instead.
Shows NumericContent including numbers, units of measurement, and status arrows indicating a trend. The numbers can be colored according to their meaning.
The Header Container with a vertical layout and with divider lines.
You can add gap between rows and columns.
Input type corresponds to the type attribute of the HTML input tag. On touch devices, it controls the keyboard layout. On desktop, the effect of this setting is browser dependent.
Here are some links. Typically links are used in user interfaces to trigger navigation to related content inside or outside of the current application.
Use of implicit static view definition.

The Horizontal Layout control is a simple way to align multiple controls horizontally. By default the contained controls are not wrapped. If you want more sophisticated layout options, consider Grid or Flex Box based layouts.
Toolbar items can be displayed depending on the current device.
Example for the different row modes
This sample demonstrates the navigation behavior of Product Switch, configurable by the app developer.
This sample demonstrates the use of a DraftIndicator in the footer area.
A tool page layout with vertical navigation
This sample represents the general usage of GridContainer.
Take advantage of sap.ui.layout.GridData to control the appearance of individual Grid children.
Dynamic Page freestyle example with a responsive sap.m.Table in the content area, showing that each control can be placed in the title and the header content areas.
Display Currencies in Table
SideNavigation with unselectable parent items.
The Vertical Layout control is a simple way to align multiple controls vertically. If you want more sophisticated layout options, consider Grid or Flex Box based layouts.
Shows how row highlights and alternating row colors can be used.
A SimpleForm that uses Toolbars as Form header and FormContainer headers.
This sample illustrates subgroups with headers, custom header and lazy loading of GridList items.
CalendarDateInterval with 14 days and single day selection
Example of a subsection displaying action buttons.
Formats and parses both integer and decimal digits.
This sample explains the formatting options of the FileSize type.
This sample explains the formatting options of the Date type with the date being available as string.
This sample explains the formatting options of the Time type.
This sample explains the formatting options of the DateTime type.
This example explains the rules for the rendering of sections
Renders whitespaces properly within controls

ResponsiveSplitter is used to visually divide the content of its parent. It consists of PaneContainers that further  agregate other PaneContainers and SplitPanes. SplitPanes can be moved to the pagination when a minimum width of their parent is reached.
This example shows how to change the default behavior in order to be able to navigate to sections instead of subsections, using the Anchor Bar
The sample shows how to set priorities of the ObjectPageHeader content items by using the ObjectPageHeaderContentLayoutData element
Toolbar handles overflow by shrinking items. OverflowToolbar provides an overflow menu. Bar is able to perfectly center a text if nothing overflows.
Flex items can be rendered differently. By default, they are wrapped in a div element. Optionally, the bare controls can be rendered directly. This can affect the resulting layout.
This is an example of Object Attribute used inside Table.
InfoLabel used in content of Table
Use the combo box dropdown list with two columns layout if you need to display additional information to your options, like e.g. currencies to countries or abbreviations to systems.

You can use the Grid control to make responsive table-free layouts; here we are using a default indent and span, and specifying the Small settings such that the image and text will stack on a small display.
With the 'footerText' property you can set a message that is shown at the very end of the list.
Display Currencies with proper Alignment
This sample shows the different states of an Object Header, which can be set using the markers.
This sample shows the different states of an Object List Item, which can be set using the markers aggregation.
Items in the ComboBox could be grouped by a property
ObjectPage sample that demonstrates the combination of header facets and showTitle properties of sections and subsections.
The Object Header is shown in condensed mode with title, number, number unit and one attribute.
This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with title and description.
Tokenizer integration with sap.m.OverflowToolbar
This sample demonstrates the inverted rendering behavior of the info text and the info state of the StandardListItem control.
Illustrates the usage of a Select with icons

An Object Header will also make space for an image if one is specified, via a URL for the 'icon' property. 
Note: This example shows the image inside ObjectHeader with the responsive property set to false. On phone in portrait mode, the image remains visible.

You can use the ‘type’ property of any list item, which inherits from ListItemBase control, to demonstrate all possible types (see sap.m.ListType). In this example, you can see the Standard List Item behavior when different values of ‘type’ property are selected.
This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with title and info.
This is a responsive Object Header without a number and with a Title, 3 Statuses/Attributes.
Table with alternating light and dark background colors. Note: The effect of this feature is only visible in some themes (e.g. SAP Belize or SAP Quartz).
A SelectList with icons.
This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with only title.
This sample illustrates how to configure the responsive settings for different container sizes.
The BlockLayout is intended to be used with rows and cells. The cells have predefined width, the rows have predefined rendering modes - scrollable/vertical/horizontal.
Shows a FixFlex control where the minFlexSize is set to 400px.
This is an example of an ObjectPageHeaderContent.
This is an example of an ObjectPageHeader containing mainly KPIs.
Shell Bar example with configured search functionality.
Shows a FixFlex control with a horizontal layout.
Calendar with minimum date 2000-01-01 and maximum date 2050-12-31, some disabled days (in January 2016) and ability to show or hide week numbers.
ToolHeader can contain IconTabHeader. When both controls are combined, the IconTabHeader supports only inline text. No icons can be used.
This layout displays a variable number of grid columns depending on available screen size. Grid row's height is dynamically determined by the height of the highest grid element on this row.
The BlockLayout Cells can have links as titles. The link text overwrites the title text.

'Single selection' forces the user to choose exactly one out of many items. With the 'multi' selection the user can pick multiple items at the same time. This is helpful for e.g. batch processing. With 'includeItem' the selection is also changed when pressing the item.
This example demonstrates the Strict layout and the column resizing of the table.

The major layout features of the Grid control are shown in this example. Features like indentation, making content visible/invisible based on the screen size, moving content forward and backwards are demonstrated.
Menu with Item Eventing
Menu with Menu Eventing
The Popover controls allows to show contextual information without leaving the current page. Press somewhere outside the popover to close it.
Use of dynamic bound model mapping
This example demonstrates how to define shortcuts using commands in your application

The initial page floorplan allows the user to navigate to a single
object to view or edit it. The interaction point on the screen is a
single input field that relies on assisted input to direct the user to
the object in as few steps as possible (using features such as value
help and live search).

The floorplan is achieved with a single sap.uxap.ObjectPageLayout with
sap.uxap.ObjectPageDynamicHeaderTitle.

sap.m.Input is used as an Input within the Title.
sap.m.MessagePage is used as a section, which informs the user
if input is needed or if the searched value is not found.
sap.m.SelectDialog is used as a value help dialog for the input.
Clicking on a link in a column opens the next column.

With the Facet Filter you can offer multiple filters ('facets') to assist the user in narrowing down the data in, say, a table. With this default 'Simple' type, each filter is displayed in a row for selection.
This sample shows a standalone feed input with different settings.
The ObjectMarker is a small building block representing an object by an icon or text and icon. Often it is used in a table.
Dynamic Page containing an sap.m.IconTabBar in the sticky subheader content area.
This example demonstrates ObjectPage with ObjectPageHeaderActionButtons and a GenericTag in the header.
An example of adding navigatable legend to the calendar.
SideNavigation with press event parameters and preventDefault.
The Nav Container stacks multiple pages and offers an API to switch between them with some animation. Typically application developers would use the App control which inherits from NavContainer.
The Responsive Popover is an abstraction of Popover and Dialog. On the phone a Dialog will be shown. On tablet and desktop a Popover is shown.
Dynamic Page demonstrating the breakpointChange event to adjust Avatar sizes responsively based on breakpoints.
Example of a subsection with showTitle property set to false.
File Uploader Example with Parameters
Example for column resizing
Basic example showing how a TreeTable can be built using a JSONModel
Button with a Badge attached
The ColorPalette in a popover (by use of thin wrapper control sap.m.ColorPalettePopover).

This is a 'light' version of the standard Busy Dialog; it also blocks the user interface until the currently running operation has been finished. It has no UI components, so you must close it programmatically when appropriate.
The customLayout aggregation determines how many pages are displayed in Carousel's visible area.
This example shows different DatePicker value states.
This example shows different DateRangeSelection value states.
This example shows different DateTimePicker value states.
This example shows Date Range Selection which is opened by another control.
This example shows Date Time Picker which is opened by another control.
This example demonstrates ObjectPage with ObjectPageDynamicHeaderTitle with Solid backgroundDesign and Translucent backgroundDesignAnchorBar.
ObjectPage sample with header content arranged using containers, called facets, ProgressIndicator and RatingIndicator.
This is an example of an ObjectPage with property alwaysShowContentHeader set to true. In this case the HeaderContent won't snap on a desktop.
Object Page sample showing a layout with subsection titles on the left.
ObjectPage sample demonstrating the breakpointChange event to adjust Avatar sizes responsively based on screen size (phone: M, tablet: L, desktop/desktop_XL: XL).
Object Page sample showing how to ensure the page is always scrolled to the top on any subsequent navigation to the page, regardless of its previously selected section in the preceding navigation.

This sample shows how bound filters work in a filter bar. As the user enters values, a toolbar with filter inputs instantly filters the customer table. It also demonstrates how to use the filter API to change the bound filters programmatically.

This sample shows how bound filters work. It features a table of customers with a 'Select' control in each row. The 'Select' control uses the customer's region to filter the list of available account managers.
Nested Splitter example with 7 content areas
The side content and the main content take 50%/50% of the container on all screen sizes except on phone screens where there is a button implemented to toggle between each other.
Example of ColorPicker in a popover using the thin wrapper control sap.ui.unified.ColorPickerPopover.
Product page with comments example.
CSSGrid example nested grids.
Example of setting customLayout for different layout (screen) sizes.

A control's field group id can be used to define a virtual group of fields that should be validated together. Field groups can be validated usinf the ValidateFieldGroup event if the user presses the enter key in a field belonging to the field group or focusses a control outside of the field group.
Creating a dialog for showing UI messages. The possible messages types are: 'None', 'Success', 'Warning' and 'Error'.
A dialog that can be toggled to fullscreen mode through a header button, by double-clicking the header, or by using the 'Shift+Ctrl+F' keyboard shortcut.
Shows the GenericTile while it is loading, if loading fails, and in disabled status.

The Growing feature helps if your content is too big to be loaded/shown at once. It paginates the content into smaller chunks - aka pages - which are loaded/shown one after another. Random access to pages (e.g jumping to the end) is not possible. Depending on the model the content is loaded on demand (OData) or shown on demand (JSON).
This example shows the container-based pop-in behavior. The container has dynamic width.

MessageBox is an easy way of displaying a message-type dialog to the user. You can display different types of dialogs:
- Types of message (Alert, Confirmation, etc.)
- Initial focus can be set to the buttons or the controls used in the message
Handle errors using the sap.m.IllustratedMessage with the error event.

Since 1.30 the value property of sap.m.TextArea is not updated on every keystroke, but first when the user presses Enter or leaves the input. The change was necessary to fully support the standard UI5 data binding with formatters and types. If you still need immediate update you have 2 options: Handle liveChange events or enable the boolean property valueLiveUpdate.
MultiComboBox with enabled Select All feature inside suggestions.
This sample explains the formatting options of the Date type with the date being available as date object.
Sample display of 'sapTheme'-prefixed CSS classes for theme-independent styling of custom HTML/Controls. The set displayed is to be used to style static HTML elements.
A sample with Message View placed inside a Dialog.
Within area of sap.ui.core.Popup determines where all popups (including popovers) are positioned.
Breadcrumbs sample with current page set as aggregation, resulting in a link
This sample illustrates the possibility to add badges to the icon tab filters.
A PDF viewer embedded in another control.
Generates MessageStrips with random properties.
MultiInput that includes a SelectDialog as a value help dialog
A control suitable for grouping notifications. The sample uses JSON data bindings.
Panels support different background designs for better visual distinction inside containers. [since rel. 1.150]
This example uses the 'sapUxAPObjectPageSubSectionTransparentBackground' CSS class to set transparent background.
A sample with Message View and inside a Dialog and grouping of items
You can have custom filters in your View Settings Dialog, as shown in this example here.
You can filter the items in the filter details page using different string filter operators.
You can have custom tabs with your own defined content in the View Settings Dialog, as shown in this example.

The View Settings Dialog is standard UI pattern for specifying sorting, grouping and filtering. For a table it should be triggered by a button in the table header with the 'drop-down-list' icon. The active filter should be shown with the table's info bar. This example also shows the context menu for the items in the Table control.
SideNavigation with a quick create action button.
SideNavigation with long texts that wrap.

An example of recommended implementation of deselection logic when the calendar is in single selection mode.
Calendar where the user can select an interval or entire week (either by selecting its week number or by using SHIFT + Space).
Calendar where the user can select multiple days, entire weeks (either by selecting its week number or by using SHIFT + Space) and ranges (using SHIFT + ENTER/Left mouse click).
Calendar with special days and legend
Basic example of Color Picker. Note that you have to set the Color Picker mode to HSL to take advantage of the responsiveness of the control on a mobile device.
Basic example of Color Picker. Note that you have to set the Color Picker mode to HSL to take advantage of the responsiveness of the control on a mobile device.
Some menu items can be added to groups to allow single or multiple item selection.
Form with one single group in a fullscreen app with a label field ratio of 3:5:4 in all sizes besides size S (12:12:0).

Form with one single group in a fullscreen app for long labels and fields, so some more space is available on medium screens (4:7:0). To avoid heavily stretched forms on extra large screens, the form gets a two-column layout in this size (4:7:0).
Form with two groups with long labels and fields in a fullscreen app.
Form with one single group in a split app with a label field ratio of 4:7:1 in all sizes besides size S (12:12:0).
A fullscreen address form with Edit / Save / Cancel in the page header, switching between a display and a change fragment; ResponsiveGridLayout arranges the columns.

Form with two groups. On large screens a two-column layout (4:8:0) is used; on medium screens a one-column layout (12:12:0); on small screens also a one-column layout (12:12:0). In the second form an empty column is displayed next to the group to be aligned with the first form.
Form with two groups, gets a two-column layout whenever possible.

Form with three groups in a three-column layout. On extra large screens a three-column layout (4:8:0) is used; on large and medium screens a two-column layout (4:8:0); on small screens a one-column layout (12:12:0).
Form with one single group in a fullscreen app using the ColumnLayout control  with default settings as layout.

Input checks are handled via the validation of the data binding. In this example there are two inputs that are validated (a) while the user types and (b) when the user continues the process. If the built-in validation types are not sufficient you can create your own, like the email type in this example.
